assumptions: Human fork F1 = (a): only a string-literal zone exempts a call ('...', "...", or a template literal with no ${}). The value is tested on argument text lexed by the shared lib/js-literals.mjs lexer, with comments and regex literals blanked and string contents blanked (a quoted 'timeZone' key keeps its text).

The `{ timeZone }` shorthand is a bare identifier, so under F1 (a) it is now FLAGGED; the #1657 test row asserting it was exempt moved to the still-flags list. This is the one intended behavior reversal of #1657.

The pin must be a top-level property of an object literal that is itself a direct argument of this call. A pin in a ternary branch, a nested object, a nested call's arguments, or behind an operator (`{ a } || { b }`) does not count.

The issue's 'remaining false negatives' (foo?.(1), make<Date>(0), fn!(0), new Date (0)) are in scope: the issue says they are cheap to fold into the same fix. A parenthesised literal is a grouping paren only when the text before it is not an identifier (other than a keyword such as return/typeof/await), `)`, `]`, `.`, `!`, or a non-arrow `>`. Accepted false positives (never negatives): `a > (5).toLocaleString()` and `!(5).toLocaleString()` now flag.
Numeric-literal exemption from #1657 is otherwise unchanged; every #1657 'does not flag' numeric row still passes.
No CHANGELOG entry: AGENTS.md does not require one per skill fix, and #1657 (the change this corrects, also unreleased) added none.
